items.title: Éogan's capricorn — a Magic sea-goat as a would-be familiar
items.context:
GM intent (not yet played): on the sea voyage home from Ireland, Éogan discovers a capricorn — a Magic-realm sea-goat (Capricornus) — that singles him out and paces his ship, drawn the same way the small fae gathered on him in Connacht, now escalated to a Might-bearing creature. Intended as a POTENTIAL familiar, not an instant bond: courting it and the binding lab-work are the actual work. Would be the first familiar prospect for any Sjórseiðr magus (directly addresses t037: no PC has bonded a familiar yet), and a payoff for the 'small fae drawn to Éogan/Stijntje' thread. Hooks to settle when activated: whether Éogan courts it, what it wants in return, and how a Magic creature relates to the faerie affinity that drew it. Realm decided: Magic. Placement: the Spring/Summer 1224 voyage home.

**DEVELOPED (session prep 2026-08-08, q027 #5).** **RULINGS:** (1) the capricorn's draw to Éogan is INDEPENDENT of any faerie affinity — it is not the same pull as the small fae of t068; a Magic-realm creature coming on its own account.
(2) What it wants in exchange for a bond is still OPEN (GM undecided).

**SIGNATURE SPECIALTY:** crossing THRESHOLDS INTO MAGICAL REGIONES — a threshold-creature that can pass (and help its bonded magus pass) regio boundaries, which makes it enormously valuable to a covenant that keeps probing regiones (Carnac, t025/t066, and beyond).

**MYTHOLOGY to draw on:** the sea-goat (goat forequarters, fish/serpent tail) is one of the oldest monsters recorded — the Babylonian 'Goat-Fish' sacred to Enki/Ea, god of fresh water, wisdom, craft and magic; overlaid in Greek myth with Pan's leap into the Nile; and, via Macrobius (a text a learned magus could know), Capricorn is the 'Gate of the Gods,' the solstitial gate through which souls ascend. The consistent motif is LIMINALITY — land and sea, the turn of the year, the boundary of the deep — which is exactly why its specialty is crossing thresholds.

**CORPUS REFERENCES for building/binding it:** familiar Bond + the three Cords (Gold=fewer botch dice, Silver=mind/mental-defence, Bronze=Soak/healing/aging) are in armdef-0.5-full.merged.ttrpg (~line 15519); Magic-creature construction (Might + Realm + Form, Magic Qualities & Inferiorities, Powers costed in Might) and a familiar-scale model are in armdef/0.4/armdef-0.4-bestiary-magical.ttrpg — e.g. the caladrius, Might 14 (Animal). NO ready-made capricorn exists in the export; it is a build-from-scratch.

**SUGGESTED BUILD (for when Éogan commits):** Realm Magic, Might ~12–16, Form Animal or Aquam (bindable by a first-timer but a genuine stretch); Powers themed to a sea-goat and to Éogan's sea magic — breathe/see through water, walk on waves / safe passage, and a regio-threshold-crossing power as its signature; likely Gift of Speech and Second Sight. A tide/weather-sensing angle would also quietly feed the maritime-hedge-tradition motif Wilhelm's thesis still lacks (t009). Directly addresses t037 (no PC magus has bonded a familiar yet).

**STATTED (2026-08-08):** a playable sheet for the CAPRICORN (Might 14 Magic sea-goat, Threshold-Walker signature) is now in npcs.json — unnamed until Éogan bonds it.

**Update (2026-08-08 session):** Advanced. Leaving for the ships near Drogheda, Éogan spotted the capricorn at a river-mouth (it favours where salt meets fresh water), took a water sample, and cast a spell to relocate the spot later. Courtship and binding still to come.

items.title: The temporal hedge mage and the brass acorn — a hedge tradition that beat the Limit of Time.
items.context:
Flagged by Wilhelm's assistants on their winter gathering-run west and south (developing q027 #1, session prep 2026-08-08). Among the traditions they turned up is a hedge mage who has genuinely MASTERED TEMPORAL MAGIC — something Hermetic theory cannot do (the Limit of Time is one of the hard walls of the Order's magic). This is both the strongest possible vindication of Wilhelm's core thesis (folk magic reaching where Hermetic theory, having stripped the context out, cannot follow — t019) and a lead worth chasing. He is also the mastered end of the road the Uisneach bird-augury only started down (reading the auspicious signal / the future, p047).

**THE DEMONSTRATION (a bootstrap paradox):** the mage 'came with' the assistants only retroactively — he claims to have attended, then didn't, and told them he had met Wilhelm IN THE FUTURE and given him a BRASS ACORN. Sure enough, Wilhelm finds a brass acorn among his things that he has no memory of packing. The acorn has no point of origin — it exists only because it already exists — which is itself the proof the mage works outside linear time. Tonally it also reassures amid the madness gut-punch: Wilhelm has a future far enough out that he and the mage meet.

**TO DEVELOP when activated:** what the brass acorn actually is (open — pure hook, an Arcane Connection to the mage, or a functional device); the mage's name, tradition, and where in the southwest the assistants found him; and whether he is a rival, a teacher (Insight for the folk system, at a price), or a cautionary example who paid a cost of his own. items.title: The Diedne Garden is a druidic circle on the Channel coast — and Valdemar's road to initiation.
items.context:
**CORRECTION OF RECORD:** the Diedne Garden lies on the SOUTH COAST OF THE ENGLISH CHANNEL. It is NOT part of the Ránargarðr holding on the Isle of Man; earlier next_session_scenes s13 text asserting that has been struck.

**WHAT IT IS:** a 3-pawn/yr Herbam vis source won in the 1223 prize draft (see resolved q003), described in the Spring 1224 harvest event as 'contested' — by whom is unrecorded and should be settled. It is an old DRUIDIC CIRCLE.

**WHY THE SITING MATTERS:** it sits in the Tribunal's heartland, not on a private island, and it was won as a Tribunal prize, so who holds it is a matter of public record. Every season Valdemar spends there is a season a Diedne site is being visited, repeatedly, by a magus from the covenant Confluensis is building a case against (t078). Part of the ordeal is simply being seen going. It also forces real seasonal competition against Undrahöll on Man (t079) and the raiding that funds it — he cannot do all three.

**THE INITIATION.** The Diedne are a thousand years dead, so there is no mystagogue: THE SITE IS THE MYSTAGOGUE. The script is kept in the circle, recoverable a rung at a time, and the Ordeals are things the place demands. Give Valdemar a DIEDNE LORE cult ability; each season in the garden is a script attempt.
  1. **THE NAMING** — Outer Mystery. He says his lineage aloud inside the ring, the first time he has said it to anything. Grants Diedne Lore 1. Minor ordeal cost.

2. **THE GREEN SEASON** — a modest grove-bound working benefit (study or spontaneous bonus within the circle).

3. **THE BENDING** — partial capstone, usable years early: reduce an opponent's Penetration by his Diedne Lore score.

4. **THE UNBROKEN RING** — Major Hermetic Virtue: HALVE an opponent's Penetration total against him.

**BALANCE / OPEN RULING.** Halving Penetration is very strong — against Penetration 40 that is a flat −20 on top of Parma. Purely defensive, so it does not warp offence, but it makes him near-unhittable by anything short of a Tribunal. Two tunings, pick one:
  **(a) BIND IT TO THE RING** — functions only inside a circle he has consecrated, including small ones laid in a season or scribed aboard a ship. Self-limiting; makes his HOLDINGS the source of his power rather than his person.

**(b) UNCONDITIONAL, PRICE IN THE FLAWS** — one Flaw per script (TMRE convention), and for a secret Diedne the right Flaws are LEGIBILITY rather than hardship: his magic begins resisting in a way no catalogued Hermetic Virtue explains. RECOMMENDED. Per t078, Confluensis's current working hunch is that Valdemar is an ORDER OF ODIN initiate, not Diedne — so an anomalous resistance does not merely expose him in general, it knocks them off the wrong theory onto the right one. The capstone virtue becomes the confession.

**STILL TO PREP:** Herbam harvest mechanics (season/window, roll, botch risk); whether a guardian, ward, or standing condition sits on the harvest; who contests it; and what the planter left behind. Valdemar means to pick up basic Herbam to work it.

items.title: Wilhelm's folk-magic integration — breakthrough scoping (Lesser Enchantments & Ceremonial)
items.context:
**GM CHEAT SHEET — How Wilhelm's integrations work mechanically.**

Because his folk magic is a hedge tradition, the right engine is Hedge Magic Revised's Insight → Integration (not the generic Bonisagus 'Original Research,' which differs slightly — see the note at the end). The loop:

1. **GAIN AN INSIGHT.** Each season he studies a source of the tradition — a text, a relic (a hedge wizard's lab/enchantment counts), or a teacher — and rolls Int + Magic Theory vs. Ease Factor 18 (Inventive Genius +3; a Gifted teacher can assist, adding their Int + Hedge Theory). Success = one Insight (and a shareable Insight Lab Text). Failure = try again later. Botch = a false insight he only discovers when the effect fails. (A teacher supplies Insights equal to their Hedge-Theory score per Breakthrough; a text/relic usually gives one each.)

2. **CREATE THE EFFECT.** Each Insight fixes one specific effect at a set level (you/troupe decide the effect — pick ones that advance the saga). He invents it in the lab with experimentation. If the level is beyond his current Lab Total, he first raises the Lab Total.

3. **AWARD POINTS** — the 'when' and 'how many': on successfully creating that effect, he gains breakthrough points equal to the effect's magnitude (level ÷ 5, round up — e.g. a level-25 effect = 5 pts, a level-40 = 8), even if it comes out warped. Then he needs a fresh Insight before the next.

4. **ACCUMULATE to the target.** Rule-of-thumb thresholds: Minor 30 / Major 45 / Hermetic 60 — you set the exact number secretly and may nudge it; the player shouldn't know it.

**HOW LONG:** budget ~2+ seasons per point-cycle (an insight season + an invention season, plus failed EF-18 rolls and any Lab-Total raising). A Minor integration ≈ 3+ years of lab time; a Major ≈ 5–10+ years. Bigger effects bank points faster but demand a higher Lab Total (and risk more Warping).

**SCOPING HIS TWO:** Ceremonial magic (props + prepared spaces, Societates 58–60) — a real non-Hermetic method → full Integration (Minor-to-Major, your call on the target). Lesser Enchantments — the pieces listed (enrich a Thing of Virtue, RoP:M p.125; vis transfer) already exist RAW, so there's little/no breakthrough to buy unless he's after a genuinely new capability; the '~20 points' figure isn't a RAW tier.

**NOTE:** the HoH:TL Bonisagus 'Original Research' variant awards points when a discovery is stabilized rather than when the effect is created — for a hedge-tradition integration, use the Hedge-Magic 'award on effect creation' version above.

**DECISION:** set the (secret) breakthrough targets for Wilhelm's integration goals.

The direction to develop: combine Scarem Montem with what is happening to the SERFS — they have REDUCED the folk-casting madness/death toll BY turning it TOWARD THE DIVINE (a Divine-aligned adaptation of the ungifted folk system). The BISHOPRIC is interested but does not want the heat from LOTHARINGIA over the separatists. Possible hook: DIETRICH (Wilhelm's brother, the thesis's public voice at Cologne) writes to Wilhelm about this. Cross-refs: the thesis provenance (Hilda gave Fettelmid the Latin copy at the 1223 Tribunal), the folk-magic madness/death toll (t019 / t020 / q028), and Furtum's parens & the bishopric (t084).

**MERGED FROM c029 (Scarem Montem kept Wilhelm's thesis for a year, deploying it against Montverte's villeins):**
**PROVENANCE (already in canon).** At the 1223 Tribunal, Hilda gave FETTELMID of Scarem Montem the LATIN copy of Wilhelm's folk-magic thesis for a 'cursory appraisal by end of day Friday.' Hilda's own plan went no further than swinging by the tent to assess whether extended review was warranted. Scarem Montem left Montverte with the manuscript in their baggage and nobody chased it. t020 already describes the situation as Wilhelm retrieving his 'stolen thesis' — this entry records what they did with it.

**THE YEAR.** By Wilhelm's Summer 1224 delivery run (s6) they have held the text roughly twelve months: replication over Fall 1223, first field deployment by Winter/Spring 1224, casualties on the ground before he sails. A year is more than enough to have independently found the madness rate that Carl and Isaac found (see q028) — and they continued. That is the moral distinction between them and Wilhelm.

Bridget of Scarem Montem pitched Éogan on the Lotharingian Tribunal at the 1223 Tribunal; destabilising Montverte's mundane base weakens the liege ahead of the Grand Tribunal petition. Run it as a GIFT rather than an experiment: the technique offered to selected villeins as folk wisdom, in villages they want turned. The madness is the point and it is deniable, because it presents as the countryside going strange on Montverte's watch.

**WHY THEY STILL WANT A HANDOVER.** A formal delivery LAUNDERS THE POSSESSION — it makes Wilhelm author of record and the transmission consensual and witnessed. A later quaesitorial inquiry then finds a Hermetic magus who gave it freely in payment of a debt. The swap is a signature, not a purchase.

**WILHELM'S COUNTER-WEAPON.** Teaching the ungifted is his exposure; it is also theirs, at scale, with intent, against mundanes. He holds a real charge.

**THE LOOSE VERIFIER.** JULIANA ex Bonisagus at Dragon's Rest holds the Low German copy and expects to swap for the Latin post-Tribunal. She does not know it has been in the field for a year. A Bonisagus, at a covenant Montverte is trying to poach, who can detonate this with no PC involvement.

entries.title: Old Harbormaster Priest
entries.note: Tends a shrine near the docks to St. Nicholas. Grizzled and fond of gin, but devout. Hears more confessions than anyone in Bruges, and keeps a coded book of what he learns — supposedly to "pray more effectively."

entries.name: Francois Malvoisin
entries.title: Antiquarian and Book Dealer
entries.note: Gnarled like the driftwood he collects, hoards texts and scraps of lore in his riverside shop. May have connections to Hermetic redcaps but denies all knowledge of magic.

entries.name: Greet of the Orchard
entries.title: Elder Sex Worker Turned Healer
entries.note: Once a famed courtesan, now runs an herbal bathhouse for women. Offers charms and quiet advice. Knows who's coming and going in the pleasure district and keeps coded symbols on her entry door each night.

entries.name: Hendrick Lamoen
entries.title: Night Watchman and Rat-Catcher
entries.note: Unkempt, paranoid, always armed with a lantern and spiked cudgel. Claims he's seen a "man with mirrored eyes" walking the rooftops at midnight.

entries.name: Ingrid of the Mire
entries.title: Fae-Touched Midwife
entries.note: Her eyes reflect moonlight even during the day. Always knows when someone is pregnant — and sometimes what the child will be. Fears "a boy born with iron in his mouth."

entries.name: Isko of Reval
entries.title: Runaway Baltic Sailor
entries.note: Towering and soft-spoken, speaks broken Flemish and better Latin. Trying to disappear in Bruges after stealing a precious charm from his former captain. Superstitious and wary of magic.

entries.name: Jakob d’Ypres
entries.title: Rival Dock Foreman
entries.note: Gruff and territorial. Hates magic, hates taxes, hates poets. Recently fired a man for "asking too many questions about river routes to Dinant." Keeps a ledger under his bed — some pages removed.

entries.name: Jan de Brakel
entries.title: Guild Master of the Carpenters
entries.note: Burly and thick-fingered, sawdust permanently in his beard. Secretly sheltering a Tytalus apprentice who fled his master.

entries.name: Judicratix Margriet van Heule
entries.title: Chief Schepen
entries.note: Sharp-tongued, always veiled, entirely incorruptible (or so she insists). Keeps notes in a personal cipher. Jurisdiction over property disputes, thefts, and "disruptions of civic peace." Suspects something unnatural in the canals.

entries.name: Klaas the Candle-Boy
entries.title: Lantern Escort and Listener
entries.note: Hired to walk clients home safely at night, mostly silent and watchful. Exceptional memory for faces and footsteps. Recently saw someone matching Valerian's description leaving with "two monks with hard hands."

entries.name: Lady Joan of Constantinople
entries.title: Countess of Flanders
entries.note: Elegant and intense, rules from Ghent, but her envoys keep a sharp eye on Bruges. Rarely seen in person, but every major noble in Bruges is either trying to support or subvert her. Secretly seeking magical aid to secure her lineage — perhaps a Hermetic opportunity.

entries.name: Lady Ysabel van Aardenburg
entries.title: Merchant Matriarch
entries.note: Sharp-witted and impeccably dressed in Flemish silks, controls a powerful wool and dye trading house. Polite but fiercely protective of Bruges' autonomy from foreign nobles.

entries.name: Lisette the Bold
entries.title: Madam of the Gilded Fig
entries.note: Raven-haired and iron-willed, runs the most luxurious brothel in Bruges. Her girls are trained in song, wit, and secrets. Valerian once performed here — Lisette keeps a lock of his hair.

entries.name: Madame Lieve
entries.title: Owner of the Crimson Duck Inn
entries.note: Witty, middle-aged, always one step ahead. Her tavern is a crossroads for gossip, illicit deals, and out-of-town couriers. Knows how to listen without seeming to.

entries.name: Maeva the Windkeeper
entries.title: Barge Captain
entries.note: A Breton woman with a raven tattoo and hair in iron rings. Sails under no banner and fears no storm. Rumors say her ship can sail even with torn sails — and that she once kissed a selkie.

entries.name: Magister Lambert
entries.title: City Scribe & Notary
entries.note: Impeccably organized, ink-stained fingers, bland expression. Quietly records all disputes, taxes, and legal matters. May have access to intercepted letters or Duke Brabant's agents' missives.

entries.name: Marthe aux Cendres
entries.title: Local Wise Woman (Cunning Folk)
entries.note: Lives in a peat-hut on the edge of the marshes. People claim she speaks with ghosts and cures madness. The local clergy are suspicious, but none dare move against her openly.

entries.name: Pieter van Cleeff
entries.title: Canal Boatman and Informant
entries.note: Wiry and grinning, knows the waterways better than anyone. Trades in rumors, contraband, and the occasional missing person.

entries.name: Ragna “the Guilder”
entries.title: Fence & Secret Broker
entries.note: A large, laughing woman with scarred hands and fine clothes. Brokers secrets as easily as smuggled goods. Keeps a circle of loyal thugs and a hidden tunnel beneath her shop.

entries.name: Roeland the Roper
entries.title: Ropemaker and Smuggler
entries.note: Broad-shouldered and cheerfully profane. His ropes are prized by sailors — but some include knotted symbols only certain buyers understand. Secretly a courier for Etienne the Dustwalker.

entries.name: Sir Rombout de Noyon
entries.title: Commander of the Castellan's Guard
entries.note: Noble-born, self-righteous, disdainful of commoners. Trains his men like soldiers, tolerates no insubordination, and has "special permission" from Duke Brabant to act outside Bruges' charter. May be directly tied to Valerian's disappearance.

entries.name: Sister Annelies
entries.title: Abbess of the Veiled Heart
entries.note: Warm but commanding, tends to fallen women and abandoned children. Known for sharp negotiation with the city's merchants. Whispers say she once healed a blind beggar — who immediately fled the city.

entries.name: Tomkin “The Little Lord”
entries.title: Effeminate Companion
entries.note: Dressed in velvet and blush, caters to nobles and scholars alike. Collects poetry, keeps a diary disguised as a songbook. Knows Valerian personally — calls him "heart-sigh." Will trade knowledge for a new gown.

entries.name: Willem de Lichtervelde
entries.title: Court Scribe & Informant
entries.note: Thin, quiet, invisible at most gatherings. Records confessions, trial outcomes, civic pronouncements. Known to pass quiet bribes to ensure charges "go missing." Might help the players — for the right cause or price.

entries.name: Baron Arnulf van Maele
entries.title: Stoic Elder Noble, House van Maele
entries.note: Proud, frost-haired, and blunt. Supports Bruges' civic independence and funds local hospitals and churches. Loyal to Countess Joan. Believes in alliances with Hermetic magi, but keeps it very discreet.

entries.name: Sir Odo van Aerschot
entries.title: Knight and Diplomat, House van Aerschot (Brabantine loyalists)
entries.note: Young, well-dressed, venomously polite. Suspected to be behind several disappearances in Bruges — including Valerian's. Maintains a suspiciously large household guard and discreetly meets with Church figures.

entries.name: Lady Ermengarde van Ruddervoorde
entries.title: Dowager with Ambition, House van Ruddervoorde
entries.note: Wears silks from Outremer, drinks heavy wine, speaks in riddles. Hosts salons where songs, lies, and truths blur. Once patronized Valerian, and may still mourn his absence.

entries.name: Diederik van Aardenburg
entries.title: Young Lord-in-Waiting, House van Aardenburg
entries.note: Hot-headed and eager to prove himself. Dabbles in fencing, philosophy, and potentially Hermetic ideas. Might become an ally or pawn depending on the party's approach. Kin to Lady Ysabel van Aardenburg.

seaFae.title: Sea Fae Bestiary
seaFae.note: Deep-sea fae, organized by ocean depth. Meant to feel alien and incomprehensible the deeper you go — GM reference for anything involving the covenant's fae/merfolk entanglements (Rán, Ka'wa'ill, Marina).

poem.title: The Depths Hold Many Names
stanzas:
The winds at play on silvered tides,
The gilded lords of mist and spray.
They dance and weave, they trick and smile,
But do not trust their fleeting guile.

Below them dine the drowned kings
and with them sailors lost at sea
Their table welcomes every guest
Should forfeit they a memory.

The weavers sing, and braid their net
To bind the lost and keep the dead
A tangled gift, a silken grave,
Swim not where memory calls the wave.

Amidst the dark a flicker's gleam,
A gentle voice, a waking dream.
Follow soft and follow bright,
And never, never see the light.

False currents pull where maps have lied,
A hungry path, the shifting tide.
One moment west, one moment none,
And when you turn, your home is gone.

The Molt-Sworn shed, their shells remain,
Hollow things with clicking frames.
An aura of them may abide
But nothing in them true resides

Drifters glow with absent thought,
Long tendrils trace what time forgot.
To take your breath, to taste the past,
And leave you sinking, thoughtless, glass.

The beggars bound deep whisper low,
In chains of tides they twist and flow.
They call for hands, they beg for keys,
Bound for cause, eternally,

Wells of black a gaping maw,
To them foolish prey they draw
They do not move, they do not wait,
But pull you down to share their fate.

The cold gods dream beyond all years,
They watch through waves, they dream your fears.
They see not flesh, they hear no cry,
A inhuman sympathy belied

Light and shadow, each must stay,
Far from where the still ones lay.
For what sleeps deep beneath the tide,
Knows no master, spares no guide.

zones.name: Epipelagic Zone (0–200m) — The Surface Lords
zones.description: These fae interact with sailors, islands, and storms — still comprehensible, but capricious.

entities.name: The Drowned Kings
entities.description: Ghostly faerie rulers of lost ships who command floating graveyards of wrecks. See the ocean as their kingdom of the dead; their courts hold banquets of drowned sailors.

entities.name: Wave Riders
entities.description: Horse-like fae that gallop across the surface of the water, sometimes carrying ships or luring them into unreachable faerie regios.

zones.name: Mesopelagic Zone (200–1000m) — The Sunken Courts
zones.description: Half-visible, bioluminescent, aware of the world above but bound to the twilight below.

entities.name: The Netweavers
entities.description: Living, sentient fishing nets that ensnare not just fish but souls and memories. Sailors who drown in them live on as whispering ghosts in their fibers.

entities.name: The Flickerlights
entities.description: Predatory fae resembling dancing lights in the darkness. Trick divers into following them into deep trenches where they vanish forever.

entities.name: The False Currents
entities.description: Shapeless fae that mimic trade winds and currents, leading ships off course into forgotten, unmapped waters.

zones.name: Bathypelagic Zone (1000–4000m) — The Abyssal Emperors
zones.description: No sunlight reaches here. Massive, ancient, slow-moving; their consciousness stretches over centuries.

entities.name: The Molt-Sworn
entities.description: Crab-like fae that continuously molt and regrow, leaving behind empty, animated husks of themselves. Trade skins and identities — some say magi who bargain with them can shed their age, for a price.

entities.name: The Dream Drifters
entities.description: Jellyfish-like fae that weave dreams into their tendrils, consuming memories and thoughts instead of flesh. The deeper you go, the more likely you are to forget why you came.

entities.name: The Leviathan-Bound
entities.description: Prisoner-gods of the deep, shackled by unknowable entities. Some escaped from Faerie, some from Hell — they'll promise anything to be freed.

zones.name: Abyssopelagic Zone (4000–6000m) — The Sleeping Ones
zones.description: Barely awake, existing in vast timeless slumber — but if disturbed, could shift entire oceans.

entities.name: The Black Wells
entities.description: Entire trenches that are actually immense fae-beings, their bodies forming undersea canyons and ridges. Those who swim too close hear voices calling them deeper.

entities.name: The Cold Gods
entities.description: Massive, slow-moving creatures entirely wrapped in darkness, sensing only by vibration and thought. See through time rather than space, and might react to the magi's search for vis long before it happens.

zones.name: Hadal Zone (6000m+) — The Unfathomable
zones.description: Barely fae at all — concepts of hunger, pressure, and stillness given form.

entities.name: Jörmungandr's Corpse
entities.description: Off the coast of Norway, in the deepest part of the sea, lies the roughly 27km-long corpse of Jörmungandr, long since transformed into a kind of magical petroleum saturated with vis. Anything sapient below the mesopelagic is a stretch to assume, but this is the exception.

entities.name: The Last Maw
entities.description: A being that does not move, yet its mouth is always open. Devours the shadows of those who pass; those who lose their shadow eventually cease to exist.

entities.name: The Final Pact
entities.description: A faerie deeper than any known depth, which will grant any wish in exchange for something you don't yet know you have.

criamonRiddles.title: Criamon Riddles & Answers
criamonRiddles.note: A shallow and a deep answer for each of the 15 Hermetic Arts, in Criamon mystery-cult style — a reusable puzzle bank for Cilene of Criamon, or any other Criamon magus. Dagmar's own answers to four of these (Imaginem, Herbam, Vim, Auram) are on his character sheet, and don't always match the "deep" answer given here — that's intentional; every Criamon magus reasons their own way in.

entries.label: “I Create”
entries.riddle: From where does the sun rise when the world is shrouded in endless night?
entries.shallow: From the east, as it always has.
entries.deep: From within. Light is not given, but remembered.

entries.label: “I Perceive”
entries.riddle: If a silent man whispers a secret, who has heard it?
entries.shallow: No one, for he made no sound.
entries.deep: The silence itself holds the secret, for knowledge is not always spoken.

entries.label: “I Transform”
entries.riddle: A serpent eats its tail, becoming itself again. Did it ever change?
entries.shallow: Yes, it changed as it consumed itself.
entries.deep: No, for it was always itself. Change is only the forgetting of what was already true.

entries.label: “I Destroy”
entries.riddle: When a shadow is swallowed by the night, where does it go?
entries.shallow: It vanishes, for there is no light to cast it.
entries.deep: It becomes the night, for absence is but another form of presence.

entries.label: “I Control”
entries.riddle: Who commands the river: the mountain that births it, the valley that holds it, or the sea that swallows it?
entries.shallow: The sea, for all rivers flow to it.
entries.deep: None and all. The river commands itself, moving by nature, yet shaped by all.

entries.riddle: A bird trapped in a cage and a fish trapped in water — who is more free?
entries.shallow: The fish, for it is where it belongs.
entries.deep: Neither, for each is confined by the limits of their understanding.

entries.label: “Water”
entries.riddle: A drop of water in the ocean and the ocean in a drop. Which is greater?
entries.shallow: The ocean, for it is vast and mighty.
entries.deep: Neither, for the ocean is nothing but many drops.

entries.label: “Air”
entries.riddle: I built a house of wind, and it held my breath. Why did it collapse when I exhaled?
entries.shallow: Wind is nothing. It cannot be shaped nor hold anything.
entries.deep: The house was real, but I no longer believed in it. My breath gave it form, my doubt destroyed it.

entries.label: “Body”
entries.riddle: My finger rotted, but I am still whole. Whose body is this?
entries.shallow: It is your body still. Parts may fail, but the self remains.
entries.deep: No part is mine, only borrowed. The body is a story the soul tells, and it forgets its lines.

entries.label: “Plant”
entries.riddle: A tree that stands for a hundred years and a flower that blooms for a day — which has lived longer?
entries.deep: The flower, for it knew no waiting.

entries.label: “Fire”
entries.riddle: What is the shape of fire?
entries.shallow: It has no shape, for it moves as it pleases.
entries.deep: It is the shape of change, for it devours all yet leaves nothing behind.

entries.label: “Image”
entries.riddle: If I wear a mask and none see beneath it, do I still exist?
entries.shallow: Yes, for I am here beneath the mask.
entries.deep: No, for I am only what others perceive.

entries.label: “Mind”
entries.riddle: A thought never spoken and a word never heard — do they have meaning?
entries.shallow: No, for meaning is given by those who receive it.
entries.deep: Yes, for meaning is not in the telling but in the knowing.

entries.label: “Earth”
entries.riddle: A stone rests unmoved for a thousand years. Was it patient, or merely forgotten?
entries.shallow: It was forgotten, for stone does not think or feel.
entries.deep: It was patient, for in stillness it remembered the shape of the world before motion.

entries.label: “Power”
entries.shallow: Nothing, for the infinite has no bounds.
entries.deep: Itself, for infinity is a circle, ever turning upon its own path.
